messages:
scanner-bot: Automated image scan detected new high/critical findings in our base images: CVE-2026-4821 (OpenSSL TLS validation bypass), CVE-2026-4822 (glibc getaddrinfo overflow). Affects ubuntu:22.04 (libssl3, libc6) and alpine:3.18 (libcrypto, musl). Full report: https://scans.example.com/scan/1778456789 :rotating_light:
Elaine: Ack. Thanks. Any evidence of active exploit in the wild?
Sam: Not seeing active exploitation in our telemetry. CVE-4821 has public PoC reported this morning though. Exploitability: medium->high for public endpoints.
Mike: Which of our services are most exposed? Hosted API, streaming endpoints, and webhooks likely highest risk. Dedicated/private customers might be fine if pinned older images, but we still should offer patched images.
Elaine: Prioritization suggestion: 1) hosted API runtime images 2) gateway images (ingress/proxy) 3) worker/sidecar images 4) customer-provided pinned images (notify). Agree?
Jon: From compliance POV we need an audit trail for rebuild/deploy decisions and customer notifications for Dedicated within 48h if we change images. Also record CVE triage notes in the tracker.
sre-oncall: FYI the canary cluster is free to use for a 2-hour soak tomorrow morning.
Sam: Plan proposal: - Trigger rebuilds with updated distro packages (Ubuntu: apt only-upgrade; Alpine: apk upgrade) - Publish new tags with suffix "-sec2026-03" and keep old tags for rollback - Run the full e2e + latency + TLS regression suite on canary - Canary rollout: 1% -> 10% -> 100% over ~3 hours if green.
Mike: CI changes: need a job that runs vulnerability scanner on resulting image and fails build on residual criticals. I'll add job: image-rebuild-and-scan. Also add Dockerfile guard: `--no-install-recommends` and clear apt lists to minimize surface.
Sam: Example Dockerfile snippet for ubuntu base builds:
```
FROM ubuntu:22.04
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --only-upgrade openssl libssl3 libc6 --no-install-recommends && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
```
Alpine snippet:
```
FROM alpine:3.18
RUN apk update && apk upgrade openssl musl && rm -rf /var/cache/apk/*
```
Elaine: Quick note: libssl package names vary by distro. Test the actual binary versions (`openssl version` and `ldd --version`) post-rebuild.
Sam: Rollout plan for Hosted: - Stage (internal) run: Tomorrow 08:00 UTC (canary cluster) - 1% traffic: 09:00 UTC (2h soak) - 10%: 11:00 UTC - 100%: 14:00 UTC. I'll prepare a rollback runbook: `rollback-to-tag <old-tag>` that triggers immediate traffic shift and redeploys old image.
Mike: For Dedicated customers: create advisory email + docs page with image digest and instructions to opt into patched images. Default behavior: do NOT force-update pinned images without customer opt-in.
Jon: Do we need KMS/keys changes? Rebuilding images doesn't affect data encryption keys. No KMS rotation required. Just ensure the image push uses existing signing keys and record signatures in audit log.
Elaine: Action items: - Sam: kick off image rebuild pipelines and schedule canary (due: 6h) - Mike: add CI scan+gate, update rollback job (due: 8h) - Jon: prepare compliance note & customer advisory draft (due: 12h) - Elaine: update CVE tracker entry and post summary in #security-notify (due: 3h)
Sam: I'm starting builds now. Will post build IDs when available.
Mike: +1. I'll wire in the scanner results to the rollback gating.
Jon: I'll draft the advisory and ping legal for the wording.
Elaine: Thanks. Keep updates here. If anything shows TLS regression in staging abort immediately and notify oncall. :eyes:
sre-oncall: Acknowledged. I'll monitor alerts and page if we see any TLS handshake failures during canary.
scanner-bot: New build scan summary for image: `redwood/api-runtime:sec2026-03-001` - no remaining criticals, 2 medium (non-exploitable in runtime), report: https://scans.example.com/build/abcd1234
Sam: Build IDs: abcd1234 (ubuntu runtime), ef56gh78 (alpine worker). Starting canary deploy to staging now.
Mike: Deploy note: add health-check grace period + extended liveness probe for first 10 minutes to avoid noisy restarts.
Elaine: Marking this triage as "mitigated-in-progress" in the tracker. Will follow up with post-deploy summary. :thumbsup:
